name: RSSHub
description: RSSHub generates RSS feeds for sites that do not offer them - social networks, video platforms, shops, forums, news outlets and hundreds more, through community-maintained route definitions. Feed the resulting URLs into any reader such as FreshRSS, Miniflux or CommaFeed.

notes.text: The instance is open to anyone who can reach it. If it is exposed beyond your LAN, uncomment ACCESS_KEY in /opt/rsshub.env and append ?key=... to your feed URLs, otherwise strangers can use your server to scrape third-party sites.

Caching goes to the local Redis with a 300 second expiry. Many routes scrape HTML, so a short cache means more requests to the target site and a higher chance of being rate-limited or blocked - raise CACHE_EXPIRE if a route starts failing.
Routes that need credentials (some social networks) are configured through additional environment variables in /opt/rsshub.env - see the route documentation upstream.
The build is a large TypeScript project and takes several minutes; 4 GB RAM is the practical minimum for it to complete.
